examples.text: C’est gros comme un rôti de famille nombreuse, rouge viande tout comme, soigneusement saucissonné dans l’épaisse couenne de ses langes, c’est luisant, c’est replet de partout, c’est un bébé, c’est l’innocence.
Je ne peux pas saucissonner mon gosse au vélo, c’est maltraitant.

glosses: Couper en fines tranches, en lamelles.
Couper en plusieurs sous-parties.

examples.text: Nous avons saucissonné toutes les mesures favorables de pouvoir d’achat dans le temps. C’était justifié par la situation des finances publiques, mais manifestement ça n’a pas été compris.
On ne peut pas saucissonner les rues avec autant de voies qu’il y a de modes de transport, actifs ou motorisés.
Nous voilà donc saucissonnés comme jadis selon notre statut socio-économique ou, si vous préférez, notre classe sociale. Eh oui! les classes sociales, ça existe encore.

glosses: Prendre un petit repas improvisé avec ce qu’on a sous la main (par exemple du saucisson).

examples.text: Vlaski, pendant ce temps, saucissonne rayon charcuterie.

glosses: That which is thin and broad.

examples.text: I pulled in hand over hand on the cord, and when I judged myself near enough, rose at infinite risk to about half my height and thus commanded the roof and a slice of the interior of the cabin.

glosses: A thin, broad piece cut off.

examples.text: a slice of bacon; a slice of cheese; a slice of bread
Jim was munching on a slice of toast.

glosses: An amount of anything.

examples.text: Blackpool, chasing a seventh win in 17 league matches, simply could not contain Sunderland's rampant attack and had to resort to a combination of last-ditch defending, fine goalkeeping and a large slice of fortune.

glosses: A piece of pizza, shaped like a sector of a circle.

examples.text: For breakfast, lunch, or dinner, the best Guido meal is a slice and a Coke.

glosses: A snack consisting of pastry with savoury filling.

examples.text: I bought a ham and cheese slice at the service station.

glosses: A broad, thin piece of plaster.
A knife with a thin, broad blade for taking up or serving fish; also, a spatula for spreading anything, as paint or ink.
A salver, platter, or tray.

A plate of iron with a handle, forming a kind of chisel, or a spadelike implement, variously proportioned, and used for various purposes, as for stripping the planking from a vessel's side, for cutting blubber from a whale, or for stirring a fire of coals; a slice bar; a peel; a fire shovel.
One of the wedges by which the cradle and the ship are lifted clear of the building blocks to prepare for launching.
A removable sliding bottom to a galley.
A shot that (for the right-handed player) curves unintentionally to the right. See fade, hook, draw.
A kind of cut shot where the bat makes an obtuse angle with the batter.
Any of a class of heavy cakes or desserts made in a tray and cut out into squarish slices.
A section of image taken of an internal organ using MRI (magnetic resonance imaging), CT (computed tomography), or various forms of x-ray.
A hawk's or falcon's dropping which squirts at an angle other than vertical. (See mute.)
A contiguous portion of an array.
To cut into slices.
To cut with an edge using a drawing motion.

examples.text: The knife left sliced his arm.

glosses: To clear (e.g. a fire, or the grate bars of a furnace) by means of a slice bar.
To hit the shuttlecock with the racket at an angle, causing it to move sideways and downwards.
To hit a shot that slices (travels from left to right for a right-handed player).
To angle the blade so that it goes too deeply into the water when starting to take a stroke.
To kick the ball so that it goes in an unintended direction, at too great an angle or too high.

examples.text: Chris Brunt sliced the spot-kick well wide but his error was soon forgotten as Olsson headed home from a corner.

glosses: To hit the ball with a stroke that causes a spin, resulting in the ball swerving or staying low after a bounce.
Having the properties of a slice knot.
